hook_2s: 9: Model updated. Memo and deck still wrong. names a familiar tie-out problem immediately; the three file tiles make it understandable with sound off.
purchase_objections: I see accepted changes, but I do not see the flagged slide corrected inside the original deck.
Does it find every dependent reference, or only the obvious text replacements?
Why does reducing DACH Q4 from 8.9 to 8.5 produce an FY26 outlook above the old range?
Will my existing charts and formatting survive the edits?
Is the coordination across my actual files enough to justify another tool alongside the AI tools I already use?
would_try: yes — The real cross-file changes and visible approval controls earn a trial on a copy of one of my packs.
buy_decision: TRY_FIRST — I am not yet convinced enough to pay after a trial because the film proves approval of proposed edits without showing that the original flagged slide is now correct.

issues.evidence: At 00:25 the panel says All changes reviewed and 10 of 10 changes accepted, but the slide with David's circled €71–73m box never returns corrected.
issues.suggested_action: Once the pending recording exists, replace part of the acceptance hold with the real original slide showing its title and flagged box both at €74.6m; retain enough of the panel to establish acceptance.

issues.evidence: The Excel bar shows Revenue!E6 8.9 → 8.5, while Word replaces €71–73m with €74.6m. No visible request identifies DACH Q4 or explains how these changes belong to one task.
issues.suggested_action: Use the captured request before the diffs and a readable caption identifying DACH Q4 8.9 → 8.5 and revised model outlook €74.6m; avoid implying that the reduction alone explains the higher outlook.

issues.evidence: Introducing Diffs promises changes across your files, followed by separate Excel, Word and PowerPoint crops. The shared workspace is never clearly established; sound off, these could look like three separate add-ins.
issues.suggested_action: Replace part of the definition card with a real workspace view containing the three file tabs and grouped Changes panel, captioned Your model, memo and deck. One workspace.

issues.evidence: Not your deck. is followed by Hers and The chat's, although no woman has been introduced. I have to decode whose files these are instead of immediately recognising my own template problem.
issues.suggested_action: Label the comparison Your existing deck and The chat's download, with a headline such as Now rebuild your deck.

issues.evidence: The closing Request early access follows another accept-or-reject definition. It gives me a signup action but little sense of what I would evaluate first.
issues.suggested_action: Keep the single Request early access CTA and replace the repeated definition with Bring your model, memo and deck. Review the changes together.

constraint_failures.rule: One task, one number, start to finish: DACH Q4 to 8.5 → FY26 €74.6m.
constraint_failures.evidence: The visible Excel change is identified as Revenue!E6 rather than DACH Q4; the initiating request is absent, and the sequence ends on acceptance status rather than the corrected flagged slide.

top_revision: Close David's specific complaint with a real post-acceptance view of the same original slide, showing the circled outlook corrected to €74.6m.
